state.app: TheDoormanFallacy.com is a free public website with no login. It explains Rory Sutherland's doorman fallacy: judging a job by its most visible task, replacing that task, and losing the work nobody wrote down. It keeps a ledger of real cases where organisations reduced roles because AI or automation was to do the work, and follows what happened afterwards. Nothing on it costs money.

state.app: TheDoormanFallacy.com is a free public website with no login. It explains Rory Sutherland's doorman fallacy: judging a job by its most visible task, replacing that task, and losing the work nobody wrote down. It keeps a ledger of real cases where organisations reduced roles because AI or automation was to do the work, and follows what happened afterwards. Nothing on it costs money.
state.place: This website, read on a visit made for the reader's own work.
state.person: You kept your job in a support team after half of it was cut when an AI assistant was introduced six months ago. You now handle the cases the assistant passes on, which are the most complicated and the angriest. Your manager reports that cost per contact has fallen.

state.app: TheDoormanFallacy.com is a free public website with no login. It explains Rory Sutherland's doorman fallacy: judging a job by its most visible task, replacing that task, and losing the work nobody wrote down. It keeps a ledger of real cases where organisations reduced roles because AI or automation was to do the work, and follows what happened afterwards. Nothing on it costs money.
state.place: This website, read on a visit made for the reader's own work.
state.person: You have spent forty minutes trying to correct a wrong charge on your phone bill. The company's chat assistant keeps answering a different question, and you cannot find a way to reach a person. You are searching online for how to reach a human there, and whether others have the same problem.

state.app: TheDoormanFallacy.com is a free public website with no login. It explains Rory Sutherland's doorman fallacy: judging a job by its most visible task, replacing that task, and losing the work nobody wrote down. It keeps a ledger of real cases where organisations reduced roles because AI or automation was to do the work, and follows what happened afterwards. Nothing on it costs money.
state.place: This website, read on a visit made for the reader's own work.
state.person: You are the chief executive of a regional insurance company with 1,200 staff. The board has asked how AI will lower costs over the next three years, and a consultancy has proposed replacing most of the claims-handling team. You approve the plan and answer to the board and the regulator for service quality.

state.app: TheDoormanFallacy.com is a free public website with no login. It explains Rory Sutherland's doorman fallacy: judging a job by its most visible task, replacing that task, and losing the work nobody wrote down. It keeps a ledger of real cases where organisations reduced roles because AI or automation was to do the work, and follows what happened afterwards. Nothing on it costs money.
state.place: This website, read on a visit made for the reader's own work.
state.person: You own a dental practice with two receptionists. A software company offers an AI phone agent that books appointments around the clock, for a monthly fee lower than one salary. Your receptionists also calm anxious patients, chase unpaid bills and know the regular patients.

state.app: TheDoormanFallacy.com is a free public website with no login. It explains Rory Sutherland's doorman fallacy: judging a job by its most visible task, replacing that task, and losing the work nobody wrote down. It keeps a ledger of real cases where organisations reduced roles because AI or automation was to do the work, and follows what happened afterwards. Nothing on it costs money.
state.place: This website, read on a visit made for the reader's own work.
state.person: You teach a course on operations and management at a business school. Each week you use real company cases for class discussion, and you prepare case notes, discussion questions and slides. You may only use material you are allowed to share with students.

state.app: TheDoormanFallacy.com is a free public website with no login. state.app: TheDoormanFallacy.com is a free public website with no login. It explains Rory Sutherland's doorman fallacy: judging a job by its most visible task, replacing that task, and losing the work nobody wrote down. It keeps a ledger of real cases where organisations reduced roles because AI or automation was to do the work, and follows what happened afterwards. Nothing on it costs money.
state.place: This website, read on a visit made for the reader's own work.
state.person: You design the customer-service AI agent at a software company that sells it to banks and retailers. You decide when the agent hands a conversation to a person, and what that person sees when it does.

state.app: TheDoormanFallacy.com is a free public website with no login. It explains Rory Sutherland's doorman fallacy: judging a job by its most visible task, replacing that task, and losing the work nobody wrote down. It keeps a ledger of real cases where organisations reduced roles because AI or automation was to do the work, and follows what happened afterwards. Nothing on it costs money.
state.place: This website, read on a visit made for the reader's own work.
state.person: Your employer, an insurance company, ended your role in its claims team three weeks ago. The company said AI tools would now handle most claims. You worked there for nine years and trained new colleagues. You are applying for jobs and preparing for interviews.

state.app: TheDoormanFallacy.com is a free public website with no login. It explains Rory Sutherland's doorman fallacy: judging a job by its most visible task, replacing that task, and losing the work nobody wrote down. It keeps a ledger of real cases where organisations reduced roles because AI or automation was to do the work, and follows what happened afterwards. Nothing on it costs money.
state.place: This website, read on a visit made for the reader's own work.
state.person: You have spent forty minutes trying to correct a wrong charge on your phone bill. The company's chat assistant keeps answering a different question, and you cannot find a way to reach a person. You are searching online for how to reach a human there, and whether others have the same problem.

state.app: TheDoormanFallacy.com is a free public website with no login. It explains Rory Sutherland's doorman fallacy: judging a job by its most visible task, replacing that task, and losing the work nobody wrote down. It keeps a ledger of real cases where organisations reduced roles because AI or automation was to do the work, and follows what happened afterwards. Nothing on it costs money.
state.place: This website, read on a visit made for the reader's own work.
state.person: You have spent forty minutes trying to correct a wrong charge on your phone bill. The company's chat assistant keeps answering a different question, and you cannot find a way to reach a person. You are searching online for how to reach a human there, and whether others have the same problem.

state.app: TheDoormanFallacy.com is a free public website with no login. It explains Rory Sutherland's doorman fallacy: judging a job by its most visible task, replacing that task, and losing the work nobody wrote down. It keeps a ledger of real cases where organisations reduced roles because AI or automation was to do the work, and follows what happened afterwards. Nothing on it costs money.
state.place: This website, read on a visit made for the reader's own work.
state.person: You teach a course on operations and management at a business school. Each week you use real company cases for class discussion, and you prepare case notes, discussion questions and slides. You may only use material you are allowed to share with students.

state.app: TheDoormanFallacy.com is a free public website with no login. It explains Rory Sutherland's doorman fallacy: judging a job by its most visible task, replacing that task, and losing the work nobody wrote down. It keeps a ledger of real cases where organisations reduced roles because AI or automation was to do the work, and follows what happened afterwards. Nothing on it costs money.
state.place: This website, read on a visit made for the reader's own work.
state.person: You teach a course on operations and management at a business school. Each week you use real company cases for class discussion, and you prepare case notes, discussion questions and slides. You may only use material you are allowed to share with students.
